The password security practice described in the text is highly insecure. Using the same password for every account is a major vulnerability because if one account is compromised, all other accounts using that same password are immediately at risk. This practice is known as password reuse. Although Sarah changes the password monthly, this does not mitigate the risk of a single breach exposing her credentials across multiple platforms. A strong security practice involves using unique, complex passwords for each account, ideally managed with a password manager.

A group of crows is called a murder.
